provenance: Self-generated for ToolDojo Live Trials: the sentences were written by ToolDojo, voiced with Microsoft Edge TTS (the voices named per clip) and resampled to 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV; the background noise is ffmpeg's anoisesrc with the fixed seed named per clip. No third-party recording is used.

sets.title: Short voice notes
sets.question: Can {tool} turn short voice notes into text you can use?
sets.limitation: The clips are four short synthetic voices reading one sentence each. Real voice notes with crosstalk, music or long pauses were not tested.
sets.takeaway_pass: if your voice notes are short and clear like these, it is worth a try
sets.takeaway_fail: check names, times and numbers by hand before you trust its notes

clips.name: The control
clips.text: Please send the final report to the design team before Friday afternoon.
clips.what: A clear American voice at a normal pace.
clips.why: This is the control: if it fails here, nothing harder will work.

clips.name: Name, time and room
clips.text: Call Maria at nine fifteen and move the budget meeting to room four.
clips.what: A name, a time and a room number in one sentence.
clips.why: These are the details a voice note exists to keep. Room four must not become room for.

clips.name: Fast British speech
clips.text: The client wants three changes: a darker logo, shorter headlines and a new contact page.
clips.what: A British voice speaking about a third faster than normal.
clips.why: People record voice notes in a hurry, and accents vary.

clips.name: Speech under noise
clips.text: Remember to back up the laptop and change the password before the trip.
clips.what: An Indian English voice under steady background hiss, only five decibels quieter than the speech.
clips.why: This is the boundary case: a noisy room is where transcription usually breaks.

sets.title: Developer jargon
sets.question: Can {tool} transcribe developer jargon without mangling it?
sets.limitation: The clips are four short synthetic voices reading one instruction each. Long technical recordings, code spelled out letter by letter and mixed languages were not tested.
sets.takeaway_pass: if you dictate short technical notes like these, it is worth a try
sets.takeaway_fail: check technical terms by hand before you paste its output anywhere

clips.name: The control
clips.text: Open the terminal, pull the latest changes and run the tests again.
clips.what: A clear American voice giving one plain instruction.
clips.why: This is the control: everyday developer words at a normal pace.

clips.name: Settings with numbers
clips.text: Set the timeout to thirty seconds and retry the request five times.
clips.what: A configuration change with two numbers in it.
clips.why: A wrong number in a setting is worse than a missing word.

clips.name: Fast Australian jargon
clips.text: The database migration failed because the schema version was older than expected.
clips.what: An Australian voice reading dense jargon about a third faster than normal.
clips.why: Words like schema and migration are rare in everyday speech, so models guess.

clips.name: Quiet speech in a noisy room
clips.text: Restart the server, clear the cache and check the error log for warnings.
clips.what: An Irish voice recorded far too quietly, with a low rumble five decibels under it.
clips.why: This is the boundary case: a quiet laptop microphone in a busy room. Cache must not become cash.
